name: Genesis AI
desc: Paris-based robotics company that trains its Eno robots on data from sensor gloves for work in factories and warehouses.
ownership: founder-owned, venture-backed (Khosla Ventures, Premji Invest, Eclipse, Nvidia, AMD, Bpifrance and others)
capacity_detail: USD 500M Series A at a USD 3.5bn valuation, co-led by Khosla Ventures, Premji Invest and Eclipse, announced 17 November 2026
markets: Plans to deploy its Eno robots in factories and warehouses; based in Paris with US and European investors

signals.raise: USD 500M Series A at USD 3.5bn valuation (Nov 2026; https://thenextweb.com/news/genesis-ai-500m-series-a-3-5bn-valuation-eno-robot)

rationale: Newly funded European robotics company; rival AI and robotics firms already use F1, and factory automation fits the sport's engineering story.

name: Rox
desc: San Francisco company whose AI agents handle research, outreach and account work for enterprise sales teams.
ownership: founder-owned, venture-backed (General Catalyst, March Capital, Sequoia Capital, GV, Databricks Ventures and others)
capacity_detail: USD 100M Series B at a USD 1.3bn valuation, co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, reported 12 November 2026
markets: Sells to enterprise sales teams; named customers include GitLab, MongoDB, Ramp, Groq, Puma Energy and Trafigura

signals.raise: USD 100M Series B at USD 1.3bn valuation (Nov 2026; https://ventureburn.com/rox-raises-100-million-ai-agents-outsell-salesforce-crm/)

rationale: Newly funded AI sales-software company selling to large enterprises; F1 hospitality reaches the commercial leaders who buy sales tools.

name: Venice AI
desc: Las Vegas company offering a privacy-focused AI assistant and developer API with access to many text, image, video and audio models.
ownership: founder-owned, venture-backed (Dragonfly, Coinbase Ventures, F-Prime Capital, North Island Ventures and others)
capacity_detail: USD 65M round valuing the company at USD 1bn, led by Dragonfly, announced 1 July 2026; its first outside funding
markets: Sold online to consumers and developers; the pages read do not break users down by country
rationale: Consumer AI brand with a privacy pitch and new funding; AI rivals already sponsor F1 teams and the audience suits a subscription product.

name: Destinus
desc: Dutch defence company making cruise missiles, interceptor drones and autonomous strike aircraft for European armed forces.
ownership: founder-led, privately held (investors not listed on the pages read)
capacity_detail: More than EUR 200M in equity raised (about USD 232M at 1.16), plus EUR 140M in convertible instruments and shareholder loans and a EUR 50M Commerzbank facility; nearly EUR 400M in total, reported 18 December 2025
markets: Supplies European armed forces; headquartered in the Netherlands with production in Europe

signals.ipo: Reportedly seeking about EUR 200M ahead of a planned Amsterdam listing (Bloomberg via The Next Web, May 2026; https://thenextweb.com/news/destinus-200-million-pre-ipo-cruise-missiles-drones)

rationale: Defence manufacturer reported to be preparing an Amsterdam listing; low consumer fit, though F1 hospitality reaches government and industrial buyers.

name: Cloudnine Hospitals (Kids Clinic India)
desc: Indian chain of maternity, fertility and children's hospitals operated by Kids Clinic India.
ownership: private: founders and private-equity investors (Permira buying 25.71% from True North)
capacity_detail: Permira agreed to buy 25.71% at a valuation of about INR 11,000 crore (about USD 1.24bn at 88.5 per dollar), per a Competition Commission of India filing reported 3 September 2026
rationale: Indian hospital chain with a new private-equity owner; a domestic consumer brand with little reason to buy global F1 rights.

name: Las Vegas Raiders
desc: National Football League team based in Las Vegas, playing at Allegiant Stadium.
ownership: private: Mark Davis (controlling owner) with minority partners including a group led by Egon Durban
capacity_detail: A group led by Egon Durban agreed to buy 25% in a deal valuing the team at USD 9.9bn, Bloomberg reported in May 2026; the sale was later approved by NFL owners
markets: United States, with NFL games and fans abroad
rationale: Las Vegas team in the city that hosts a Grand Prix; a team sells sponsorship itself, so a cross-promotion is likelier than a purchase.

name: Cleveland Browns
desc: National Football League team based in Cleveland, Ohio.
ownership: private: Haslam family (majority owners) with Arctos Partners as a limited partner
capacity_detail: Sold a stake to Arctos Partners at a valuation above USD 9bn, Bloomberg reported on 19 May 2026; NFL owners approved the 3% sale
rationale: NFL team with a mainly US audience; a team sells sponsorship itself, so it is an unlikely buyer of F1 rights.

name: Atlanta Falcons
desc: National Football League team based in Atlanta, Georgia.
ownership: private: Arthur Blank (owner) with limited partners including Arctos Partners
capacity_detail: Arctos agreed to buy 10% at a USD 10.6bn valuation, CNBC reported in August 2026; the team announced Arctos as a 7.5% limited partner in October 2026
rationale: NFL team with a mainly US audience; a team sells sponsorship itself, so it is an unlikely buyer of F1 rights.

name: Liverpool FC
desc: English Premier League football club owned by Fenway Sports Group, with one of the largest fan bases in world football.
ownership: private: Fenway Sports Group (majority) with a consortium including Jeff Bezos buying about 30%
capacity_detail: A consortium including Jeff Bezos agreed to buy about 30% for GBP 1.65bn, valuing the club at about GBP 5.5bn (about USD 7.3bn at 1.33), reported August 2026
rationale: Global football brand with new investors; a club sells sponsorship itself, so a joint promotion is likelier than a purchase.

name: New York Yankees (Yankee Global Enterprises)
desc: Major League Baseball team and its parent company, controlled by the Steinbrenner family.
ownership: private: Steinbrenner family (controlling) with Apollo as an investor
capacity_detail: USD 2.6bn financing with Apollo Sports Capital announced August 2026, a mix of debt and equity; the New York Post reported it values the team at significantly more than USD 12bn (valuation not given by the team)
markets: United States, with a brand known abroad
rationale: One of the best-known sports brands in the US; a team sells sponsorship itself, so a joint promotion is likelier than a purchase.
